subject: life-sciences
description: Life Sciences skill tree, FET Grades 10-12 (CAPS). 4 Knowledge Strands: S1 Life at Molecular/Cellular/Tissue Level, S2 Life Processes in Plants and Animals, S3 Environmental Studies, S4 Diversity/Change/Continuity. Tiers = CAPS strands within a grade. Mastery = 60% of 20-item pool (FET rule, no timer). v1.1: G10 slimmed from 32 → 25 atomic skills via 7 merges. Items live in data/life-sciences-question-bank.json.

levels.title: Grade 10 — Life Sciences
levels.description: All four CAPS Knowledge Strands. Recommended teaching order: S1 (Molecules → Cells → Tissues) → S2 (Support and Transport) → S3 (Biosphere to Ecosystems) → S4 (Biodiversity, History of Life). 25 atomic skills.

tiers.title: S1 — Life at the Molecular, Cellular and Tissue Level

atomic_skills.title: Inorganic compounds, food tests and nutritional analysis
atomic_skills.description: Water; macro/micro minerals (Na, K, Ca, P, Fe, I, nitrates, phosphates) with roles + deficiency diseases; fertilisers and eutrophication. Food tests: starch (iodine), reducing sugars (Benedict's), lipids (translucent spot), proteins (Biuret). Interpret nutritional information and compare diet vs RDA.

error_signatures.description: Confuses macro and micro mineral elements
error_signatures.example: Lists iron as a macro element
Says Benedict's turns purple for proteins

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor each mineral to one role + one deficiency. Water = solvent + transport + temperature. Eutrophication = run-off → algae bloom → O2 drop → fish die. Food tests: iodine→starch (blue-black), Benedict's+HEAT→sugars (orange), Biuret→protein (purple), translucent paper→lipids.

atomic_skills.title: Organic compounds — carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, vitamins
atomic_skills.description: Classify by element composition. Distinguish mono/di/polysaccharides; saturated vs unsaturated fats; cholesterol and heart disease; proteins as amino-acid chains sensitive to temperature and pH. Brief mention of nucleic acids and vitamins.

error_signatures.example: Says unsaturated fats cause heart disease

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mono = glucose, fructose; di = sucrose, maltose; poly = starch, cellulose, glycogen. Unsaturated = liquid at room temp, healthier; saturated + cholesterol = artery risk.

atomic_skills.title: Enzymes — properties and the Lock and Key Model
atomic_skills.description: Define enzyme as a biological catalyst (protein). Lock and Key Model. Effect of temperature and pH (denaturation). Everyday examples (biological washing powders, digestion).

error_signatures.description: Thinks high temperature always speeds enzymes up
Confuses denaturation with destruction of substrate
error_signatures.example: Says high temperature destroys the food the enzyme is digesting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Activity rises with temp UNTIL the optimum, then falls sharply (denaturation: active site changes shape). Each enzyme has an optimum pH.

atomic_skills.title: Cell structure — organelles and their functions
atomic_skills.description: Name and locate major organelles (cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, ribosomes, ER, Golgi, plastids, vacuole, lysosomes). State the function of each. Distinguish plant and animal cells.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Cells: the basic units of life

error_signatures.description: Thinks animal cells have cell walls
error_signatures.example: Says cheek cells are bounded by cellulose

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mito = energy. Chloroplast = energy capture (plants only). Cell wall = plants only. Vacuole = large in plants, small in animals.

atomic_skills.title: Cell membrane and transport — diffusion, osmosis, active transport
atomic_skills.description: Fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane. Distinguish diffusion, osmosis and active transport. Predict water movement in hypertonic, hypotonic and isotonic solutions.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Cells: the basic units of life

error_signatures.example: Says water moves from low to high water concentration
Says active transport happens down a gradient without ATP

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Diffusion = particles spread (high→low). Osmosis = WATER moves toward higher solute concentration (lower water). Active transport = against gradient, needs ATP.

atomic_skills.title: Microscopy and measuring cell size
atomic_skills.description: History of microscopy (lens → light → electron microscope) and cell theory. Calculate magnification using a scale line. Estimate field of view and cell size under a light microscope.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Cells: the basic units of life

error_signatures.description: Divides instead of multiplies in magnification formula
error_signatures.example: Says magnification = real size ÷ drawing size
Says higher magnification always means a clearer image

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Magnification = drawing size ÷ real size (same units). Resolution = detail (electron > light). High magnification + poor resolution = bigger but blurry.

atomic_skills.title: The cell cycle and mitosis
atomic_skills.description: Cell cycle (interphase, mitosis, cytokinesis). Phases (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase). Outcome: two genetically identical daughter cells. Role of mitosis (growth, repair, asexual reproduction). Plant vs animal cytokinesis.

error_signatures.description: Thinks mitosis halves the chromosome number

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PMAT: Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase. Mitosis = identical copies (2n→2n). Plants build a cell plate; animals pinch in.

atomic_skills.title: Cancer and cell-division biotechnology
atomic_skills.description: Cancer as uncontrolled cell division — causes, treatments, attitudes. Cell-division biotechnology — cloning, stem-cell research, ethics, SA legislation.

error_signatures.example: Says you can catch cancer from someone
Says clones are designed to have different genes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cancer = cells ignore the stop-dividing signal. Not contagious. Cloning = genetic copy (same DNA). Embryonic stem cells = pluripotent; adult stem cells = limited.

atomic_skills.title: Plant and animal tissues
atomic_skills.description: Plant tissues (xylem, phloem, parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma, epidermis, meristematic) — structure and function. Four animal tissues (epithelial, connective, muscle, nerve) with examples.

error_signatures.description: Swaps xylem and phloem transport roles

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Plant: Xylem=water (one-way, up); Phloem=sugar (both directions); Meristem=where cells divide. Animal: Epithelial covers, Connective supports (bone/blood), Muscle contracts, Nerve sends signals.

atomic_skills.title: Tissue biotechnology and indigenous knowledge
atomic_skills.description: Tissue-related medical biotechnology (immunity, vaccines, antibiotics, blood transfusions, in vitro fertilisation, tissue cloning). Indigenous knowledge applications (traditional healers, plant-based remedies, links to modern medicine).

error_signatures.example: Says traditional healers reject all modern medicine

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Vaccine = teaches immune system in advance (viruses + bacteria). Antibiotic = kills bacteria (not viruses). Many SA traditional remedies (Hoodia, Pelargonium) are now scientifically studied.

tiers.title: S2 — Life Processes in Plants and Animals

atomic_skills.title: Support systems in plants
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish herbaceous and woody plant support. Role of xylem (lignified secondary cell walls), sclerenchyma and collenchyma. Turgor pressure as support in soft plants.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Support and transport systems in plants

error_signatures.description: Thinks all plants need wood for support
error_signatures.example: Says lettuce stands up because of lignin
Says animal cells get support from turgor

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Soft plants stand by water pressure (turgor). Woody plants stand by lignified xylem. Loss of water → wilting (loss of turgor).

atomic_skills.title: Plant transport and transpiration
atomic_skills.description: Structure of xylem (vessels, tracheids) and phloem (sieve tubes, companion cells). Transpiration as water-vapour loss; transpiration pull theory. Translocation in phloem. Environmental factors affecting transpiration (light, temperature, humidity, wind).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Support and transport systems in plants

error_signatures.example: Says phloem transports water from roots to leaves
Says wet air pulls more water out of leaves

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Xylem = WATER, root→leaf, one-way. Phloem = SUGAR, both directions. Transpiration rises with light, temp, wind; falls with humidity.

atomic_skills.title: Animal support — the human skeleton
atomic_skills.description: Functions of the skeleton (support, protection, movement, blood-cell formation, mineral storage). Axial vs appendicular skeleton. Structure of long bones and joint types.

error_signatures.example: Says blood is made in the heart

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Axial = skull, ribs, vertebrae (centre line). Appendicular = limbs + girdles. Long bones: compact outside, spongy inside, marrow makes blood cells.

atomic_skills.title: Bone disorders and indigenous knowledge of plant remedies
atomic_skills.description: Common bone disorders (osteoporosis, rickets, arthritis) and causes. Indigenous knowledge of plant-based treatments and links to modern medicine.

error_signatures.example: Says rickets affects only old people

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Rickets = soft bones in children (Vit D / Ca). Osteoporosis = thinning bones in adults. Arthritis = joint inflammation. Many SA traditional remedies use plant extracts now studied scientifically.

atomic_skills.title: Muscles and movement
atomic_skills.description: Three muscle types (skeletal, smooth, cardiac). Antagonistic muscle pairs (biceps + triceps). Tendons (muscle-to-bone) and ligaments (bone-to-bone).

error_signatures.example: Says tendons join bone to bone

error_signatures.description: Thinks muscles push as well as pull
error_signatures.example: Says biceps push the arm down

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tendon = muscle→bone. Ligament = bone→bone. Muscles only PULL. Pairs work in opposition.

atomic_skills.title: Heart structure, circulation and the cardiac cycle
atomic_skills.description: Label heart chambers, valves and major vessels. Double-circulation pathway (pulmonary + systemic). Why left ventricle wall is thicker. Cardiac cycle (atrial systole, ventricular systole, diastole). SA and AV nodes coordinating the heartbeat. Pulse rate and exercise.

error_signatures.example: Says blood leaves the heart through the atria
Says oxygenated blood enters the right atrium

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: RIGHT side = DEoxygenated (body→lungs). LEFT side = OXYGENATED (lungs→body). Left ventricle thicker for whole-body pump. Cycle: atria→ventricles→relax. SA node = pacemaker.

atomic_skills.title: Blood vessels, blood composition and lymph
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish arteries, veins and capillaries by structure and function. Blood components (red cells, white cells, platelets, plasma) and their functions. Lymphatic system.

error_signatures.description: Swaps red and white cell roles
error_signatures.example: Says red blood cells fight infection

error_signatures.description: Treats arteries as always carrying oxygenated blood
error_signatures.example: Says the pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Arteries: thick walls, away from heart (mostly oxygenated — pulmonary artery is the exception). Veins: thin walls, valves, toward heart. Capillaries: one-cell-thick, where exchange happens.

atomic_skills.title: Cardiovascular disease and lifestyle
atomic_skills.description: Common cardiovascular diseases (hypertension, atherosclerosis, heart attack, stroke) and risk factors. Lifestyle choices that reduce risk. Interpret blood-pressure and cholesterol data.

error_signatures.example: Says a stroke happens in the heart

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Heart attack = blocked coronary artery (heart muscle). Stroke = blocked or burst vessel in the brain. HDL = good, LDL = bad. Risk drops with no smoking, exercise, low saturated fat.

atomic_skills.title: Biosphere, biomes and ecosystems
atomic_skills.description: Define biosphere, biome and ecosystem. SA biomes (Fynbos, Grassland, Savanna, Forest, Succulent Karoo, Nama Karoo, Desert, Thicket, Indian Ocean Coastal Belt). Abiotic vs biotic factors.

error_signatures.example: Calls a single pond a biome

error_signatures.description: Treats abiotic and biotic as the same

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Biosphere = all life + non-life on Earth. Biome = large climate-life region. Ecosystem = community + its abiotic environment. Abiotic = non-living; Biotic = living.

atomic_skills.title: Energy flow, food chains and food webs
atomic_skills.description: Draw and interpret food chains, food webs and energy pyramids. Producers, consumers (primary, secondary, tertiary), decomposers. Why energy decreases at each trophic level.

error_signatures.description: Reverses arrow direction in a food chain
error_signatures.example: Says arrows point from predator to prey
Calls a lion a primary consumer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Arrows point in direction energy FLOWS (eaten → eater). Producer → primary → secondary → tertiary. Only ~10% energy passes up each level.

atomic_skills.title: Nutrient cycles — carbon, nitrogen, water
atomic_skills.description: Carbon, nitrogen and water cycles. Human disturbances at key steps (deforestation, fossil-fuel combustion, fertiliser use).

error_signatures.example: Says nitrification removes nitrogen from soil

error_signatures.description: Thinks plants take nitrogen from the air directly
error_signatures.example: Says plant roots absorb N2 gas

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Carbon: photosynthesis ↔ respiration + combustion. Water: evaporation → condensation → precipitation. Nitrogen: fixation (N2→NH3 by bacteria) → nitrification (→NO3⁻) → uptake → denitrification (→N2).

atomic_skills.title: Ecological field study and seasonal change
atomic_skills.description: Design a simple ecological field study (abiotic + biotic factors). Compare seasons. Explain succession.

error_signatures.example: Compares two sites with different soil type and different light without flagging it
Says succession is birds flying away

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Field study: list abiotic + biotic factors, sample the same way, repeat across seasons. Succession = orderly replacement over time (pioneer → climax).

atomic_skills.title: Biodiversity, taxonomy and binomial naming
atomic_skills.description: Define biodiversity. Taxonomic hierarchy (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species). Five-kingdom system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia). Use binomial nomenclature correctly (Genus species, italicised). Apply a simple dichotomous key.

error_signatures.description: Doesn't capitalise the genus or italicise the name

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mnemonic: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup. Genus capitalised, species lowercase, both italic: *Homo sapiens*. Dichotomous key gives two choices at each step.

atomic_skills.title: South African biodiversity and conservation
atomic_skills.description: SA as a megadiverse country. Cape Floral Kingdom (Fynbos) as a global biodiversity hotspot. Threats (habitat loss, invasive species, poaching, climate change). Conservation responses (national parks, CITES, Red List).

error_signatures.description: Misses Fynbos as a biodiversity hotspot
error_signatures.example: Names Savanna as SA's most diverse biome

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Endemic = found ONLY in one place. Endangered = at risk of extinction. SA's Cape Floral Kingdom is the smallest of the six floral kingdoms but most species per area.

atomic_skills.title: History of life, mass extinctions and South African fossil sites
atomic_skills.description: Define a fossil and how they form. Order major events in life's history. Five major mass extinctions and causes. SA fossil sites — Karoo (Permian-Triassic), Cradle of Humankind (Sterkfontein, Malapa, Naledi — hominins).

error_signatures.example: Says modern mammals evolved before dinosaurs

error_signatures.description: Thinks all extinctions were caused by asteroid impacts
error_signatures.example: Says the end-Permian was an asteroid

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Simple cells (3.8 Gya) → photosynthesis → O2 → Cambrian explosion (~540 Mya) → dinosaurs (Mesozoic) → mammals (Cenozoic). End-Permian (252 Mya) = biggest (volcanic). End-Cretaceous (66 Mya) = killed dinosaurs (asteroid).

levels.title: Grade 11 — Life Sciences
levels.description: Grade 11 covers Strands 2 (Life Processes), 3 (Environmental Studies) and 4 (Diversity, Change and Continuity). CAPS teaching order: S4 first (microorganisms → plants → animals), then S2 (energy + nutrition + respiration + gas exchange + excretion), then S3 (population ecology + human impact). 23 atomic skills.

atomic_skills.title: Classification of microorganisms — viruses, bacteria, protists, fungi
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish the four microbe groups by cellular features. Viruses (acellular, protein coat + nucleic acid). Bacteria (prokaryote, no nucleus). Protists (eukaryote, mostly single-celled). Fungi (eukaryote, chitin walls, absorptive). Examples for each.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Virus = no cell. Bacteria = prokaryote (no nucleus). Protist = eukaryote single-celled. Fungi = eukaryote chitin walls + absorptive feeding.

atomic_skills.title: Microorganisms in disease, food and biotechnology
atomic_skills.description: Microbe-caused diseases (TB, cholera, HIV/AIDS, malaria, COVID-19). Beneficial microbes in food (sorghum beer, amasi, bread, cheese). Antibiotics + resistance. Vaccines. Sewage treatment.

error_signatures.example: Says TB is caused by a virus

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TB = bacterium (Mycobacterium tuberculosis). HIV = virus. Cholera = bacterium. Malaria = protist (Plasmodium). Antibiotics target bacteria. Vaccines train the immune system.

atomic_skills.title: Bryophytes and pteridophytes — mosses and ferns
atomic_skills.description: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) — no vascular tissue, no true roots, need water for fertilisation. Pteridophytes (ferns) — vascular, true roots/stems/leaves, still need water for fertilisation. Alternation of generations.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mosses = no vascular, no real roots (rhizoids), water for fertilisation. Ferns = vascular but still no seeds, spores. Both need water for sperm to swim to egg.

atomic_skills.title: Gymnosperms and angiosperms — seed plants
atomic_skills.description: Gymnosperms (cycads, conifers) — naked seeds in cones, no flowers. Angiosperms — flowering plants with seeds in fruits. Monocots vs dicots. SA examples (cycads, fynbos, Marula, indigenous trees).
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Gymnosperm = naked seeds in cones (pines, cycads). Angiosperm = seeds in fruits (most plants). Monocot: 1 cotyledon, parallel veins, fibrous roots. Dicot: 2 cotyledons, net veins, tap root.

atomic_skills.title: Flower structure and pollination
atomic_skills.description: Parts of a typical flower (sepals, petals, stamens with anther/filament, carpel with stigma/style/ovary). Types of pollination (wind, insect, bird). SA pollinators (sunbirds, carpenter bees, beetles, bats).
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Male = stamen (anther + filament). Female = carpel (stigma + style + ovary). Wind-pollinated = small/dull/no nectar. Insect/bird-pollinated = colourful, nectar, scent.

atomic_skills.title: Fertilisation, fruit, seed and dispersal
atomic_skills.description: Double fertilisation in angiosperms (zygote + endosperm). Fruit develops from ovary; seed develops from ovule. Seed structure (embryo, food store, testa). Types of seed dispersal (wind, water, animal, explosive). Germination conditions.

error_signatures.example: Says only one sperm cell is involved

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ovary → fruit. Ovule → seed. Double fertilisation: 2 sperm cells = 1 makes zygote, 1 makes endosperm. Germination needs water + warmth + O2.

atomic_skills.title: Invertebrate phyla — main groups
atomic_skills.description: Major phyla: Porifera (sponges), Cnidaria (jellyfish, sea anemones), Platyhelminthes (flatworms), Nematoda (roundworms), Annelida (segmented worms), Mollusca (snails, octopus), Arthropoda (insects, crustaceans), Echinodermata (starfish). Distinguishing features + SA examples.

error_signatures.example: Says insects are a separate kingdom

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Arthropods = exoskeleton + jointed legs (insects, spiders, crabs). Molluscs = soft body, often shell (snail, octopus). Annelids = segmented. Echinoderms = five-fold radial symmetry (starfish).

atomic_skills.title: Chordates — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals
atomic_skills.description: Phylum Chordata: notochord, dorsal nerve cord. Classes: Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia. Defining features, evolutionary transitions, SA examples.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Fish = gills, fins, scales. Amphibian = moist skin, larvae in water. Reptile = scales, lay eggs on land, cold-blooded. Birds = feathers, warm-blooded, beaks. Mammals = fur, milk, warm-blooded.

tiers.title: S2 — Life Processes in Plants and Animals

atomic_skills.title: Photosynthesis — process and pigments
atomic_skills.description: Chloroplast structure (thylakoids, stroma, grana). Light-dependent reactions (light + water → ATP, NADPH, O2). Light-independent reactions / Calvin cycle (CO2 + ATP + NADPH → glucose). Overall word equation. Chlorophyll a, b, and accessory pigments.

error_signatures.example: Says Calvin cycle needs light directly
Claims oxygen comes from carbon dioxide splitting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Light reactions: in thylakoids, water split → O2 + ATP + NADPH. Calvin cycle: in stroma, CO2 fixed using ATP/NADPH → glucose. O2 comes from water, NOT CO2.

atomic_skills.title: Photosynthesis — limiting factors and applications
atomic_skills.description: Light intensity, CO2, temperature, water as limiting factors. Interpret rate-of-photosynthesis graphs. Greenhouse use (CO2 enrichment, controlled temperature). Importance for SA food security.

error_signatures.example: Names CO2 even when light is clearly limiting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Limiting factor = the one in short supply that holds back the rate. Plot rate vs each factor — the flat plateau tells you which factor is limiting and which isn't.

atomic_skills.title: Human digestive system — structure and processes
atomic_skills.description: Mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus. Mechanical + chemical digestion. Enzymes (amylase, pepsin, lipase, trypsin). Absorption in villi. Role of liver and pancreas.

error_signatures.description: Thinks the stomach absorbs all nutrients
error_signatures.example: Says food is absorbed in the stomach

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Amylase (saliva, pancreas) → starch. Pepsin (stomach) → protein. Lipase (pancreas) → fat. Absorption mainly in the small intestine via villi (huge surface area).

atomic_skills.title: Balanced diet, malnutrition and diet-related diseases
atomic_skills.description: Food groups + their roles. Balanced diet principles. Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency), marasmus (energy + protein deficiency), obesity, type 2 diabetes. SA public-health context. Reading food labels.

error_signatures.example: Says kwashiorkor is total energy deficiency

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Kwashiorkor = protein deficiency, swollen belly, hair changes. Marasmus = both energy + protein lacking, severe wasting. Obesity + Type 2 diabetes = excess + poor diet.

atomic_skills.title: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration
atomic_skills.description: Aerobic respiration: glycolysis → Krebs → ETC. Overall equation. Anaerobic respiration: lactic-acid fermentation in muscle; alcohol fermentation in yeast. ATP yields. Mitochondrial role.

error_signatures.example: Says anaerobic respiration gives more ATP

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Aerobic = needs O2, ~36 ATP, CO2 + H2O. Anaerobic = no O2, only 2 ATP. Muscles → lactic acid. Yeast → ethanol + CO2 (alcohol fermentation).

atomic_skills.title: Respiration vs photosynthesis; exercise effects
atomic_skills.description: Compare respiration and photosynthesis (reactants, products, location, energy flow). How they connect in living systems. Effects of exercise: increased breathing, heart rate, sweating. Oxygen debt and recovery.

error_signatures.example: Says oxygen debt cannot be repaid

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Plants do BOTH — photosynthesise (day) AND respire (24/7). Oxygen debt = the extra O2 needed after exercise to oxidise the lactic acid built up.

atomic_skills.title: Gas exchange in mammals — lungs and ventilation
atomic_skills.description: Respiratory pathway: nose/mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Ventilation mechanism (intercostal muscles + diaphragm). Gas exchange across alveolar wall + capillary wall. Adaptations of alveoli (surface area, moisture, thin wall, blood supply).
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Inhalation: diaphragm contracts (flattens), intercostals contract, chest volume up → pressure drops → air rushes in. Exhalation: opposite. Alveoli features: 1-cell-thick + moist + huge area + capillaries.

atomic_skills.title: Gas exchange in plants, fish and insects
atomic_skills.description: Plants: stomata for CO2/O2 exchange in leaves. Fish: gills with countercurrent flow. Insects: tracheal system (spiracles, tracheae, tracheoles). Surface-area-to-volume principle.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Plants: stomata (mainly underside of leaf). Fish: gills (gas-rich water flows opposite blood = countercurrent). Insects: tracheae deliver O2 directly to cells (no blood transport).

atomic_skills.title: Kidney structure and the nephron
atomic_skills.description: Kidney location, renal artery and vein. Nephron structure (Bowman's capsule, proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, collecting duct). Three processes: ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, secretion. Urine formation.

error_signatures.example: Says glucose is filtered out and not reabsorbed

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ultrafiltration in Bowman's capsule = blood squeezed → filtrate. Reabsorption in proximal tubule = useful stuff back (glucose, salts, water). Secretion = extra waste added.

atomic_skills.title: Excretory disorders and treatments
atomic_skills.description: Kidney failure causes (diabetes, hypertension, infection). Symptoms. Dialysis (haemodialysis, peritoneal). Kidney transplants. Lifestyle factors. SA access to dialysis context.

error_signatures.description: Thinks kidney damage is reversible always
error_signatures.example: Says you can repair kidneys easily

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Dialysis = machine filters blood (does kidney's job). Transplant = donor kidney implanted. Major SA causes: diabetes + hypertension. Prevention = control BP, blood sugar, hydration.

atomic_skills.title: Population growth and limiting factors
atomic_skills.description: Birth rate, death rate, immigration, emigration. Exponential (J) and logistic (S) growth curves. Carrying capacity. Density-dependent vs density-independent factors. Quadrat and mark-recapture sampling.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: J-curve = unlimited resources, exponential. S-curve = approaches carrying capacity (K). Density-dependent: more crowded = more limiting (disease, food). Density-independent: same effect regardless of density (storms, fire).

atomic_skills.title: Community ecology and species interactions
atomic_skills.description: Predation, competition (intra/inter), parasitism, mutualism, commensalism. Niche concept. Ecological succession (primary, secondary). SA examples (lion–zebra, fynbos succession, mycorrhizae).

error_signatures.description: Thinks two species can share an identical niche

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mutualism = both benefit. Commensalism = one benefits, other unaffected. Parasitism = one benefits, other harmed. Predation = one eats the other. Competition = same resource.

atomic_skills.title: Atmosphere — greenhouse effect, climate change and ozone
atomic_skills.description: Natural vs enhanced greenhouse effect. Main greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, water vapour). Sources of human emissions. Consequences: warming, droughts, sea-level rise, ocean acidification. Ozone-layer depletion (CFCs). SA-specific impacts.

error_signatures.description: Confuses greenhouse effect with ozone depletion
error_signatures.example: Says CFCs cause global warming directly

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Greenhouse = traps heat (CO2, CH4). Ozone depletion = upper atmosphere thinning (CFCs). They are DIFFERENT problems — though both human-caused atmospheric harm.

atomic_skills.title: Water, soil and alien invasive species
atomic_skills.description: Water pollution sources (sewage, fertilisers, industrial). Eutrophication recap. Soil erosion + overgrazing. Alien invasive species (Black Wattle, Port Jackson, water hyacinth) and their water/biodiversity costs.

error_signatures.example: Says alien plants don't affect water supply

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Alien invasive = brought from outside, spreads aggressively, harms ecosystems. SA Working for Water programme clears them — saves water + restores indigenous vegetation.

atomic_skills.title: Biodiversity loss and South African conservation responses
atomic_skills.description: Drivers: habitat loss, overharvesting (rhino, abalone), invasive species, climate change. SA conservation responses: SANParks, CapeNature, Working for Water, Wildlife Act, CITES. Flagship species. Sustainable use.

error_signatures.example: Says private people can't help conservation
Places Cape Floral Kingdom in Limpopo

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SA conservation = government (SANParks, CapeNature), NGOs (WWF-SA), communities, private land. CITES regulates international trade in endangered species. Demand reduction is also key.

levels.title: Grade 12 — Life Sciences
levels.description: Grade 12 covers Strands 1 (Molecular/Cellular — DNA/RNA/Meiosis), 2 (Life Processes — Reproduction, Nervous, Endocrine, Homeostasis) and 4 (Diversity — Evolution, Human Evolution). Strand 3 (Human Impact) is taught in Gr11 but examined in NSC at end of Gr12 — learners revising for matric should reference G11 IMP.A1–A3. 22 atomic skills.

tiers.title: S1 — Life at the Molecular, Cellular and Tissue Level

atomic_skills.title: DNA structure and the genetic code
atomic_skills.description: Double helix; nucleotide structure (sugar, phosphate, base); base pairing A-T, G-C; Chargaff's rules; antiparallel strands.

error_signatures.example: Says bases form the sugar-phosphate backbone

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Double helix = two strands twisted. Backbone = sugar (deoxyribose) + phosphate. Bases inside: A-T (2 bonds), G-C (3 bonds). Strands run opposite directions (antiparallel).

atomic_skills.title: DNA replication
atomic_skills.description: Semi-conservative replication; DNA helicase, polymerase, leading and lagging strand basics; why exact copying matters.

error_signatures.example: Claims both old strands stay together

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Semi-conservative = each new molecule has 1 old + 1 new strand. Helicase unzips. Polymerase adds bases to match. Result: 2 identical DNA molecules.

atomic_skills.title: Transcription and translation
atomic_skills.description: RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA); transcription (DNA → mRNA); translation (mRNA → protein at ribosome); codon table; one gene → one polypeptide.

error_signatures.example: Says protein is made in the nucleus
Says every base codes for protein

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Transcription: DNA → mRNA (in nucleus). Translation: mRNA → protein (at ribosomes in cytoplasm). Codon = 3 mRNA bases = 1 amino acid.

atomic_skills.title: Mutations and genetic conditions
atomic_skills.description: Point mutations (substitution, deletion, insertion); frameshift; sickle cell, albinism, Down syndrome; mutagens (UV, smoke, radiation).

error_signatures.example: Says a deletion is a point mutation in the strict sense
Says no mutation is ever beneficial

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Point = one base. Frameshift = insertion/deletion that shifts the reading frame. Some mutations are neutral or beneficial; most harmful or neutral.

atomic_skills.title: Meiosis — process and stages
atomic_skills.description: Meiosis I (homologous chromosomes separate) and II (sister chromatids separate); crossing over (prophase I); reduction division (2n → n); independent assortment.

error_signatures.example: Says sister chromatids separate in meiosis I

error_signatures.description: Thinks meiosis = mitosis with extra step
error_signatures.example: Says daughter cells are genetically identical

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Meiosis I = HOMOLOGUES separate (reduction). Meiosis II = SISTER CHROMATIDS separate (like mitosis). End result: 4 genetically different haploid cells.

atomic_skills.title: Significance of meiosis and chromosomal abnormalities
atomic_skills.description: Meiosis generates genetic variation (crossing over + independent assortment + fertilisation). Non-disjunction → trisomy/monosomy. Down syndrome (trisomy 21). Importance for evolution.

error_signatures.description: Wrong chromosome number for Down syndrome

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Meiosis = variation (3 sources). Non-disjunction = chromosome stays with sibling → trisomy or monosomy. Down syndrome = trisomy 21 (extra copy of chromosome 21).

tiers.title: S2 — Life Processes in Plants and Animals

atomic_skills.title: Reproduction in vertebrates — strategies
atomic_skills.description: External vs internal fertilisation; oviparity, ovoviviparity, viviparity; parental care; r-selection vs K-selection.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: External = fish/amphibians in water. Internal = reptiles/birds/mammals. Oviparous = lays eggs. Viviparous = live young. K-selection = few offspring + much care. r-selection = many offspring + little care.

atomic_skills.title: Human reproductive anatomy
atomic_skills.description: Male: testes, epididymis, vas deferens, prostate, seminal vesicle, penis. Female: ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, vagina. Gamete production.

error_signatures.example: Says fallopian tubes are in males
Says eggs are made in the uterus

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sperm made in testes (continuously). Eggs released from ovaries (monthly). Fertilisation in fallopian tube. Implantation in uterus.

atomic_skills.title: Menstrual cycle, fertilisation and pregnancy
atomic_skills.description: Menstrual cycle phases (menstrual, follicular, ovulation, luteal); hormones (FSH, LH, oestrogen, progesterone); fertilisation; implantation; pregnancy; birth.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 28-day cycle: Day 1 = menstruation; ~Day 14 = ovulation; Day 28 = end. FSH grows follicle, LH triggers ovulation, oestrogen and progesterone build up the uterus.

atomic_skills.title: Contraception and STIs
atomic_skills.description: Contraceptive methods (barrier, hormonal, IUD, sterilisation, natural). STIs: HIV/AIDS, gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydia, HPV. SA epidemiology. Prevention.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Condom = pregnancy + STI. Pill = pregnancy only. HIV = virus, ARV treatment + U=U. Many STIs are bacterial (curable with antibiotics).

atomic_skills.title: Central nervous system — brain and spinal cord
atomic_skills.description: Brain parts: cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla oblongata, hypothalamus. Functions of each. Spinal cord. Meninges. CSF.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cerebrum = thinking/voluntary. Cerebellum = balance/coordination. Medulla = heartbeat/breathing. Hypothalamus = temperature/water/hormones.

atomic_skills.title: Neurons, reflex arc and nervous disorders
atomic_skills.description: Neuron structure (dendrites, cell body, axon, myelin). Sensory, motor, relay neurons. Synapse. Reflex arc. Common disorders (Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, MS).

error_signatures.example: Says motor neuron comes before sensory
Says you 'decide' to pull hand away

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Reflex arc: stimulus → receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord (relay) → motor neuron → effector → response. Bypasses brain for speed.

atomic_skills.title: The eye — structure, vision and defects
atomic_skills.description: Eye anatomy (cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, rods, cones, optic nerve). Image formation. Accommodation. Myopia (short-sighted), hypermetropia (long-sighted), cataracts, astigmatism.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Rods = low-light, B&W. Cones = colour. Myopia = eyeball too long → can't focus far → CONCAVE lens. Hypermetropia = too short → can't focus near → CONVEX lens.

atomic_skills.title: The ear — hearing and balance
atomic_skills.description: Ear anatomy (outer, middle, inner). Sound transmission: pinna → eardrum → ossicles → oval window → cochlea → auditory nerve. Semicircular canals = balance. Deafness causes.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sound: pinna catches → eardrum vibrates → hammer/anvil/stirrup amplify → oval window → cochlea (sound) or semicircular canals (balance).

atomic_skills.title: Endocrine system — major glands and hormones
atomic_skills.description: Hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads. Major hormones and their target effects. Negative feedback.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pituitary = master gland. Thyroid = thyroxine. Pancreas = insulin/glucagon. Adrenals = adrenaline/cortisol. Negative feedback keeps levels stable.

atomic_skills.title: Diabetes and hormone disorders
atomic_skills.description: Type 1 vs Type 2 diabetes; insulin therapy; symptoms; SA prevalence. Other disorders: goitre, dwarfism/gigantism, Addison's disease.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: T1 = autoimmune, no insulin produced, often young. T2 = insulin resistance, often middle-aged + lifestyle. Both need management. SA has rising T2 rates.

atomic_skills.title: Thermoregulation and osmoregulation
atomic_skills.description: Thermoregulation: skin response (sweating, shivering, vasoconstriction/dilation). Osmoregulation: kidney + ADH. Feedback loops.

error_signatures.description: Thinks sweating works only by water loss

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Hot: sweat + vasodilation (more heat lost). Cold: shiver + vasoconstriction (less heat lost). Dry: ADH high → small concentrated urine.

atomic_skills.title: Glucose regulation
atomic_skills.description: Insulin (lowers blood sugar — uptake + glycogen storage). Glucagon (raises blood sugar — glycogen breakdown). Negative feedback loop. Link to diabetes.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Insulin LOWERS glucose. Glucagon RAISES glucose. Both made by pancreas. Glycogen stored in liver + muscle. Feedback keeps blood sugar steady.

atomic_skills.title: Darwinism and evidence for evolution
atomic_skills.description: Natural selection: variation → struggle → survival of fittest → inheritance. Evidence: fossils, biogeography, comparative anatomy, embryology, molecular (DNA).

error_signatures.example: Says one giraffe stretched its neck

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Variation + struggle + selection + inheritance over generations. Evidence: 5 main types — fossils, biogeography, anatomy, embryology, DNA. Individuals don't evolve; populations do.

atomic_skills.title: Speciation and modern examples
atomic_skills.description: Speciation (allopatric, sympatric). Modern examples: antibiotic-resistant bacteria, peppered moth, pesticide resistance, SA examples (fynbos diversity, cichlids).
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Allopatric = geographic separation. Sympatric = same place but split (e.g. plants polyploidy). Resistance to antibiotics/pesticides = real-time natural selection.

atomic_skills.title: Hominin lineage — australopithecines to Homo
atomic_skills.description: Major hominin species: Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy), A. africanus, Homo habilis, H. erectus, H. neanderthalensis, H. sapiens. Bipedalism, brain size, tool use trends.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Australopithecines (~4 Mya) → Homo habilis (~2.5 Mya) → H. erectus (~1.8 Mya) → H. sapiens (~300 kya). We share a common ancestor with chimps, not descended from them.

atomic_skills.title: South African fossils and Out-of-Africa
atomic_skills.description: Key SA fossils: Mrs Ples (A. africanus, Sterkfontein), Karabo (A. sediba, Malapa), Homo naledi (Rising Star). Out-of-Africa theory. SA scientists' contributions.

error_signatures.example: Says Mrs Ples is Homo naledi

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mrs Ples = A. africanus. Karabo = A. sediba. Naledi = Homo naledi. Out-of-Africa: H. sapiens evolved in Africa ~300 kya, then spread globally. SA = key fossil region.
